title: SIT™ Pilot vs In-House Team — A Side-by-Side Cost Breakdown
content:
###  **Two Paths, Different Cost Structures** 

Building an in-house team means paying for hiring, training, management, and turnover before a single result appears. A pilot means paying for the output directly — consistent field activity — without any of the setup cost. 

###  **What Companies Typically Find** 

When the full cost of building independently is added up — not just wages but time, training, and management — a structured pilot is often less expensive overall, not more. 

### **Why the Comparison Rarely Gets Made** 

Most companies compare an hourly wage to an hourly rate and stop there. The real comparison includes everything it takes to get a wage-earner to become a consistent, trained, supervised performer. 

###  **Seeing It for Yourself** 

The clearest way to understand the difference is a short pilot — real weeks, real activity, a direct look at what consistent output actually costs.
